summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 61% to INR2,146 crore and PAT 59% to INR201 crore; cell line guided to lift EBITDA margin toward 20%+ later.
summary.overview: Insolation Energy listed on BSE and NSE Main Board on 9 March 2026. FY26 revenue from operations was INR2,146 crore (up 61%), EBITDA INR305 crore (up 79%, margin 14% vs 13%), and PAT INR201 crore (up 59%). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR794 crore (up 100% YoY), with EBITDA INR111 crore and PAT INR70 crore, though management said utility-scale dispatches cluster in the last month of each quarter. Management is building a 4.5 GW TOPCon cell line and 4.5 GW aluminium frame plant at Narmadapuram, with cell COD targeted for Q3/Q4 FY27 and frames in Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity / ROCE / ROE

financial_highlights.value: INR835 crore (long-term INR468 crore; short-term INR300 crore)
financial_highlights.change: from INR108 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Solar modules
segments.commentary: FY26 sales mix was about 85% non-DCR and 15% DCR. Module capacity is 5.5 GW. Management targets about 2 GW production and sales from modules in FY27, with non-DCR at 2-2.5 GW and DCR cells sourced externally on top.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Very nascent; minimal revenue in Q4 FY26. A third-party order of over INR300 crore secured last year is expected to contribute revenue in FY27.

segments.name: IPP (KUSUM)
segments.commentary: Targeting about 325 MW AC / 400 MW DC, with 38-40 MW commissioned so far. FY27 IPP revenue guided at about INR135 crore; FY28 at about INR300 crore. Capex about INR1,000 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at least equal to FY26 (about 50-60%), subject to market conditions; FY28 revenue target above INR5,000 crore.
EBITDA margin in FY27 expected at 14-15% including aluminium frame integration; management says 20%+ once the full cell line runs (FY28 framing).
FY27 capex about INR2,500 crore: about INR1,500 crore for the cell line (including working capital margin and contingency) and about INR1,000 crore for KUSUM IPP.
Positive free cash flow expected 6-8 months after cell plant goes live (Q4 FY27), per CFO.
Wafer/ingot plant (4.5 GW, CZ technology, about INR1,000-1,200 crore capex) to be funded mainly from internal accruals; DPR due in 2-3 months.
Peak debt expected near INR1,500 crore in FY27; IREDA loan of INR1,134 crore, 12-month moratorium then 7-year repayment, at 8.95% post-COD.
capex_capacity: Sawarda Unit 3 (INR320 crore) fully operational with all three lines running.

4.5 GW TOPCon cell line at Narmadapuram: INR340 crore drawn from IREDA by 31 March 2026; expected to start ramp-up in Q4 FY27, full ramp about 3-4 months later (management said full utilisation by Q1 FY28).
Aluminium frame plant (4.5 GW) expected to commission in Q1 FY27; mainly for internal use.
Next phase: 4.5 GW ingot and wafer on 70,000 sq m of land acquired in Narmadapuram; about 20 acres remain. ALMM Part 3 effective 1 June 2028 is the stated timing driver.
Cell line plant efficiency target above 80%; management says the cell capacity is used internally first, with any surplus sold in the open market.
demand_pricing: Current order book of about 1.6-1.8 GW for this year, per management; about 50% of FY27 capacity already booked, with the rest refilled monthly from distributors, OEM white-label and KUSUM partners.
Non-DCR module prices about INR13-14/W; DCR about INR20-22/W (Mono PERC INR20-21, TOPCon INR21-22, up to INR22.5 in some locations).
Sales mix by segment in FY26: utility about 65%, KUSUM about 15%, PM Surya Ghar about 5%, OEM about 5%, miscellaneous about 10%.

Raw-material cost pressure noted; management said it will pass through some increase and absorb some, relying on about 2-3 months of raw material held in inventory against orders. Escalation clauses are mostly USD-linked.
Management estimates about 30 GW of non-ALMM modules in the market, and said non-DCR cell demand remains for 1-1.5 years of tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Is there visibility on FY27 volume and margin after the cell line comes on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 2 GW module production and sales in FY27 and 14-15% EBITDA margin, rising to 20%+ with the full cell line. Ravi said margins could be revised upward if market conditions allow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did December and March not sustain the run rate of Q4 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utility-scale dispatches are concentrated in the last month of each quarter, with about INR350 crore in December and about INR440 crore in March, and that this is an industry pattern.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and debt picture after receivables rose 156%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said short-term borrowing rose because of capacity scale-up, and that orders are now on 45-day LCs, which lifts receivables. IREDA drawdown of INR340 crore is largely parked in FDs of about INR300 crore; the remaining drawdowns are expected within 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost on borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: IREDA loan sanctioned at 9.20% pre-COD and 8.95% post-COD. Working capital borrowings are close to 8%.

risks_watch: Raw-material cost inflation and the ability to pass it through, given that price escalation is mainly USD-linked and orders are priced ahead.
Cell line ramp timing (Q4 FY27 start, full utilisation by Q1 FY28); next two quarters' utilisation guided at only 60-70%.
Heavy reliance on Chinese equipment for the cell line; management cites a two-year on-site support contract with the supplier.
Quarter-end-loaded dispatches make quarterly revenue and receivables lumpy; receivables rose to INR280 crore.
Negative FCFF (CFO's FCF yield cited as -15.9%) until the cell plant is operating; peak debt near INR1,500 crore in FY27.
Wafer/ingot plant (INR1,000-1,200 crore) remains at DPR stage with no technology partner named; the CZ technology choice is still under consideration.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term growth and margins, but hedged on near-term figures, repeatedly tying guidance to market conditions. Answers were sometimes inconsistent (for example, on the FY27 margin and capex funding), and several questions had to be re-asked.
key_quotes: we definitely we assure that whatever the growth in FY 26 should be there, the revenue growth in FY27 at least should be there.
Yes, definitely, our EBITDA margin should increase when our cell is operational.
Usually the solar cell efficiencies are much higher than the modules. We are targeting for more than 80% of the plant efficiency.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of at least FY26's ~50-60% and FY28 revenue above INR5,000 crore, backed by a 1.6-1.8 GW order book with ~50% of FY27 capacity booked, a 4.5 GW frame plant due Q1 FY27 and a cell line with COD in Q3/Q4 FY27; the cell line's timing and FY28 target are still forward-looking, and the brief gives no order-level contract detail beyond the INR300 crore EPC order.
